title: Uniform Hilbert stability of smooth curves embedded by high-degree complete series
statement: Let $g\geq2$ and $d\geq2g+1$ be integers and put $r=d+1-g$. There is an integer $M(g,d)$ with the following property over every algebraically closed field $k$ [def-weil-field]. Let $C$ be a smooth projective connected curve over $k$, of genus $g=\dim_k H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-pc-genus], and let $L$ be an invertible module of degree $d$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Suppose $C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ is the embedding defined by the complete linear system of $L$, meaning a chosen identification $k^r\simeq H^0(C,L)$ and its evaluation map. For every $m\geq M(g,d)$ the Hilbert point of this embedding, with Hilbert polynomial $dm+1-g$, is stable for the Hilbert-Pluecker linearization of [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization]. The bound depends only on $g,d$, and not on $C$, $L$ or the characteristic. The scheme, invertible-module, projective and ample conventions are [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-invertible-module, def-kun-projective, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Smoothness is [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and connected curve is [def-sc-curves].

source.place: Section 2.4, Theorem 5, printed pp.10--11: uniform high-degree smooth-curve stability. Local PDF WANTED; read online.

proof.text: Put $N=r=d+1-g$. The chosen complete-series identification already gives $\dim H^0(C,L)=N$, and the specified embedding gives surjective evaluation. Fix an arbitrary full flag $V_i\subset H^0(C,L)$ with $\dim V_i=N-i$. Apply [lem-sfb-linear-series-degree-dimension-bound] to each nonzero $V_i$. Thus $A_i=\operatorname{im}(V_i\otimes\mathcal O_C\to L)$ is invertible, $0\leq a_i:=\deg A_i\leq d$, and $N-i\leq\max\{a_i+1-g,a_i/2+1\}$. Write $e_i=d-a_i$.

source.place: Theorem 5, geometric input and Figure 1, printed p.10

proof.text: For $i=0$, the full space generates $L$, so $a_0=d$ and $e_0=0$. For $i=N-1$, the subspace is one-dimensional, so its generated image is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_C$ and $a_{N-1}=0$, giving $e_{N-1}=d$. For every $i$, $0\leq e_i\leq d$. These are the endpoint and range assertions of [lem-sfb-linear-series-degree-dimension-bound]. In particular a positive strict gap cannot be imposed at the final endpoint.

source.place: Theorem 5, correction of the endpoint in the sentence before Figure 1

proof.text: Since $g\geq2$ and $d\geq2g+1$, we have $N\geq4$ and $1<\alpha:=d/(N-1)<2$. For $0<i<N-1$, the maximum inequality of Step 1 gives one of two bounds. If $N-i\leq a_i+1-g$, then $e_i\leq i<\alpha i$. If $N-i\leq a_i/2+1$, then $e_i\leq d-2(N-1)+2i$, and subtracting $\alpha i$ from this upper bound gives $(2-\alpha)(i-(N-1))<0$. Consequently $e_i<di/(N-1)$ for every interior $i$. This uses exactly the degree-dimension inequality of [lem-sfb-linear-series-degree-dimension-bound], with the two cases written out instead of the source's erroneous endpoint-wide gap.

source.place: Theorem 5, Riemann-Roch/Clifford slope argument, printed pp.10--11

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-strict-codegree-polygon-gap] with these integers $N,d$. Its hypotheses are Steps 2 and 3. It gives a single $\eta(N,d)>0$ for all admissible integral codegree tuples and all decreasing real normalized weights. Therefore every full flag on this $C$, and indeed on any curve in the statement, satisfies $B(e,w)\leq 2d/N-\eta(N,d)$. The same $\eta$ works for all curves because it depends only on $N,d$, not on the flag, subseries or field.

source.place: Theorem 5, final reduction to Lemma 6; corrected strict polygon form

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-uniform-gieseker-codegree-criterion] with $V=H^0(C,L)$ and $\epsilon=\eta(N,d)$. The curve is smooth projective connected, has the required genus and degree, and its given complete series defines the required closed immersion. Step 4 supplies the hypothesis for every full flag and every normalized weight tuple, including the rational weights from nontrivial one-parameter subgroups. The criterion gives $M_0(g,d,N,\eta)$ such that all $m\geq M_0$ have stable $\operatorname{SL}_N$ Hilbert points with polynomial $P(m)=dm+1-g$. Since $N$ and $\eta$ depend only on $g,d$, this is uniform in the curve and in the characteristic.

source.place: Theorem 5, conclusion via Lemma 4(3) and Lemma 2(3), printed pp.7--11

proof.text: Take $M(g,d)$ to be the maximum of $M_0$ and the field-independent Hilbert embedding threshold $M(P,N)$ of [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization]. That node identifies the stable loci for $(\operatorname{SL}_N,\Lambda_m)$ and $(\operatorname{PGL}_N,\Lambda_m^{\otimes N})$ in every characteristic. Thus the stability just proved is precisely stability for the Hilbert-Pluecker linearization specified in the statement, with no restriction when the characteristic divides $N$. Both thresholds depend only on $g,d$.

source.place: Section 2.1, Hilbert linearization, printed pp.4--5; item linearization convention

Source checked: Morrison, arXiv:0810.2340, pp.6-12, fetched from arXiv and converted with pdftotext. I read Prop 1, Lemma 2(3), §2.3 estimate (5), Lemma 4, Theorem 5 and Lemma 6. The worker's two source errors are both real. (a) In Theorem 5, the claim ε_j=(d/(N-1)-δ)(j-1) fails at j=N, because V_N is one-dimensional and has codegree d. (b) Lemma 6 is off by a factor of two: w=(1/2,1/3,1/6,0) with N=4 gives a minimum of 3/2, above the printed 3/4. The correct bound is 2(N-1)/N.

Steps 1-3 hold under the RR/Clifford maximum bound, with N>=4 and 1<α=d/(d-g)<2. In the Clifford case the gap is (2-α)(i-(N-1))<0. On g=2, d=5 the bounds are e_1<=1 and e_2<=3, and hyperelliptic g^1_2 subseries attain them.

Step 4: the hypotheses of the polygon node match exactly. I proved that node independently: the lower convex envelope gives cost <=2d/N, equality forces the linear chord, and inserting an interior index lowers the cost by w_0(αi-e_i)>0. Compactness and finitely many e give a uniform η. For N=2 the claim fails, so N>=3 is the right hypothesis.

Step 5: the normalized Gieseker criterion is Lemma 4(1)/(3) with Σw=1, and it is not a restatement of the item.

Step 6: lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization gives a k-independent threshold and equal SL/PGL stable loci in every characteristic.

The linear-series node is true: Clifford for 0<=a<=2g-2, RR for a>=2g-1, and the q=1 and complete-series clauses hold. None of the three new nodes duplicates an existing node (rg for Clifford, codegree, Gieseker and numerical criterion). There are no SGA citations, no off-unit tools and no fixes. Advisory: the maintainer should add the local PDF of arXiv:0810.2340 to literature/.
